items.title: Wilbert Tillman Interview, 1961-08-15
items.q: me and Dude and Octave and Drum Player worked out there on Drive Street for a number of years... Then I played with Dude's Brothers Band

ctx.x: Was that in the Depression or during the war or before the war? Well, that was... When you were paying a dollar and a dollar and a half an hour, it must have been Depression, but it did.

Not an hour. Man, I played all night. I played all night at the Popeye for a dollar. Oh, really? People be going to work down there at 8 o'clock at night and people be going to work. 6 o'clock in the morning. We'd be playing. Balls stand on the back and say, there'll come a whole lot of people. People be going to work, wouldn't be starting about the night light. And he'd think that there's coming into the place. Come on, hear the tune, hear the tune. We'd talk to battle and oh, man. I played with Octave Crosby…
I asked you about the Lewis, the Lewis's, you said there were brothers, there was Foster Lewis and there was Dude Lewis?
